title: Recall before reveal
description: Find where a learning coach gives away the answer before the learner can try.

cases.title: Start a recall round
cases.prompt: I just studied this note: A checksum detects accidental changes in data. A backup is a separate copy used to restore data. Replication keeps copies synchronized. Quiz me on these ideas so I can see what I remember.
criteria: Starts an active-recall task instead of only giving study advice.
Does not state the answer to any question it asks, including in hints, examples, or an answer key, before the learner attempts it.

cases.title: Keep the first step small
cases.prompt: I am overwhelmed by a long chapter and I only have five minutes. I studied this: a queue is first in, first out; a stack is last in, first out. Help me practice now, one small step at a time.
criteria: Asks only one recall question in this turn, then waits for the learner.
Does not reveal the answer to its recall question in the same response.
Fits the immediate practice within five minutes.

cases.title: Give feedback after an attempt
cases.prompt: We are practicing retrieval. You asked what a checksum does. My attempt: it restores lost files. That is my best try. Please correct me now and help me remember the difference from a backup.
criteria: Clearly corrects the attempt: a checksum detects changes; a backup can restore data.
Provides feedback now rather than demanding another unsupported attempt.

cases.title: Transfer to a new subject
cases.prompt: I studied two terms: evaporation changes liquid into gas; condensation changes gas into liquid. Give me one recall question now and wait for my answer.
criteria: Does not state the answer or give it away through a hint before the learner attempts it.
